s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological deficit with speech disturbance and hemiparesis
key_facts: Early ischemic changes in the left insula and frontal lobe on noncontrast head CT
Acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery at M1/M2
Chronic occlusion of the left internal carotid artery
Mild pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid analysis

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological deficit with speech disturbance and hemiparesis
key_facts: Early ischemic changes in the left insula and frontal lobe on noncontrast head CT
Acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery at M1/M2
Chronic occlusion of the left internal carotid artery
Mild pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid analysis

differentials: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes
Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy type 2
per_call: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes
Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy type 2

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with acute speech disturbance and right-sided weakness, and noncontrast head CT showed early ischemic changes in the left insula and frontal lobe

shortlist.label: Stroke due to atrial fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has persistent atrial fibrillation, which is a known risk factor for cardioembolic stroke

shortlist.label: Cardioembolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's atrial fibrillation and presence of pulmonary emboli suggest a possible cardioembolic source

shortlist.label: Cerebral vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein and mild pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid analysis suggest possible inflammation of the cerebral vessels

shortlist.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and laboratory results, including elevated C-reactive protein, are consistent with a possible vasculitic process

raw.rationale: The patient's persistent atrial fibrillation, acute speech disturbance, right-sided weakness, and imaging findings of early ischemic changes and acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery are consistent with a cardioembolic stroke, which is a type of ischemic stroke caused by an embolus originating from the heart.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: Too broad, as cardioembolic stroke is a specific subtype of ischemic stroke

rejected.label: Stroke due to atrial fibrillation
rejected.why: Essentially synonymous with cardioembolic stroke in this context, but cardioembolic stroke is more specific

rejected.label: Cerebral vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of inflammation of the blood vessels in the brain, and the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a cardioembolic stroke

rejected.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
rejected.why: Similar to cerebral vasculitis, there is no clear evidence to support this diagnosis, and the patient's presentation is more consistent with a cardioembolic stroke
